title: Platform admin console (/admin): multi-tenant ops UI
description:
## Why
Operators need app.withlanyard.com/_platform (or equivalent) to manage secrets, integrations, OAuth, skills, and tenant/instance config across company brains — without SSH/SM hand edits. Today the monorepo has no shipped super-admin SPA; /_platform returns the tenant SPA shell. Control Plane APIs + SM/wake inject already cover much of the backend.

## Scope (no Daytona sandbox requirement for core ops)
1. Dual-auth: platform operator identity separate from tenant users
2. Platform admin SPA + CF routing for /_platform/*
3. BFF/admin API gate → private CP (+ secrets materialize / wake inject)
4. Secrets & model/connector CRUD (incl. POOLSIDE_API_KEY / XAI / OAuth slots) → SM or material store → next wake
5. Tenant / instance / roles / audit surfaces over existing CP routes
6. Policy for host-local skills/integrations (wake materialize vs online Brain RPC)

## Non-goals
- Replacing tenant Settings for end users
- Baking tenant vault into snapshots

Refs: docs/architecture/end-to-end-architecture.md (super-admin not shipped); lp-kng.7 model inject residual
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Design doc: auth plane, routes, secrets flow, CF behaviors
- [ ] /_platform SPA distinct from tenant app; operator login works
- [ ] Cross-tenant secret/key set visible to ops; lands on next agent wake inject
- [ ] Tenant list/instances/roles via CP; no raw CP public exposure
- [ ] Staging proof without requiring Daytona for admin-only paths
notes: Both implementation children done+shipped (lp-2qs.4 #601, lp-2qs.5 #602). 2026-08-24 live staging verification (no Daytona): /admin ops console deployed and serving on app.withlanyard.com; /api/admin/* auth plane live — CSRF mint OK, Google OAuth 302 with signed ops state, all ops data routes fail-closed 401 unauthenticated. Remaining: operator allowlist env PLATFORM_OPERATOR_EMAILS unset on live BFF task def :43, so sign-in would 403 — filed lp-2qs.6 for Jack to add his operator email + complete sign-in proof (cross-tenant secret set visible to ops).

description:

Rules:
1. already_online: no create/start/mount work
2. start-from-stopped: entrypoint ensure-mounted is idempotent — no-op if Mountpoint already up; remount only if FUSE lost (expected after stop)

4. Pre-bake: mount-s3 binary in snapshot; S3 prefix+seed at provision; never rewrite s3_vault_prefix on wake
5. Explicitly reject: Daytona Volumes as Lanyard vault durability; remount tax on every ensure_online while online

title: Daytona vault: idempotent guest ensure-mounted (no remount tax on every wake)
description:
## Why
MockLab Brain RPC is on, but Directory/Vault/projects fail:
- vault.tree roots=[] (source=brain_rpc)
- projects.create → EACCES mkdir /mnt/vault/Demo
- S3 seed exists under tenants/{id}/vault/ but is not visible in guest

Root cause (2026-08-06 live): guest /mnt/vault is an empty root-owned local dir. Entrypoint waits for a readable path and starts the gateway without Mountpoint. CP injects VAULT_ROOT + S3_VAULT_PREFIX but live sandboxes lack LANYARD_VAULT_BUCKET and STS; volumes=[]. Closed work (lp-hjo, lp-3en, lp-b7w, lp-3a1.5) left metadata/env path incomplete for real guest mount.

## Product constraint (human)
Do NOT pay a full S3 mount ceremony on every ensure_online / every cold create as the default. Wake must be as fast as possible:
- already_online → zero mount work (FUSE already up)
- start-from-stopped → idempotent ensure-mounted (no-op if up; fast remount only if FUSE lost)
- cold create → first mount once before gateway; pre-bake mount-s3 in snapshot (no install-on-boot)

Daytona cannot pre-attach Lanyard customer S3 natively. Daytona Volumes are not Lanyard vault durability. Pre-do off hot path: snapshot tools, provision prefix+seed, durable s3_vault_prefix. Tenant vault contents are not baked into a shared snapshot.

## Locked approach
1. Guest **ensure-mounted** (entrypoint helper): if already mounted → return immediately; else mount-s3 with inject env/creds.
2. Pre-bake mount-s3 in agent snapshot.
3. CP inject LANYARD_VAULT_BUCKET + short-lived scoped STS when a remount is required (create and start paths that re-enter guest boot).
4. Agent user can write under VAULT_ROOT.
5. Pilot: prefer keeping sandbox started after first good mount; stop orphan sandboxes sharing instance_id.
6. Prove MockLab vault.tree, projects.create, S3 durability after stop/start remount of same prefix.

Evidence: artifacts/daytona-pilot/vault-projects-diagnosis/RESULT.md
Plan anchors: docs/plans/0008-daytona-agent-sandboxes/{overview,gateway-env-contract,spike-3en,spike-bnd,s3-vault-prefix-layout}.md

## Out of scope for this epic
- Platform multi-tenant model/connector admin UI (sibling residual)
- Guest working-set cache (lp-eto.2, deferred)
- brain.health on LA (separate small residual if needed)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Documented wake cost model: already_online / start-stopped ensure-mounted / cold first-mount; no remount on already_online
- [ ] Snapshot includes mount-s3; entrypoint ensure-mounted is idempotent
- [ ] Live MockLab: vault.tree shows S3 seed; projects.create succeeds under /mnt/vault; write visible in S3
- [ ] already_online path does not re-run mount work
- [ ] Orphan multi-sandbox for same instance_id cleaned or prevented
- [ ] Evidence under artifacts/daytona-pilot/ (sanitized)
